robot.name: Reachy Mini
robot.status_notes: Announced and available for order July 9, 2025, starting at $399 Lite and $499 Wireless. Company states delivery about 90 days. User comments on the official launch post indicate some orders from December 2025 were still awaiting shipment as of March-April 2026.

height.notes: Official product page lists 11"/28cm. Tech Times reported 'two feet tall' which conflicts; official value used here.

payload.notes: No payload capacity published; desktop robot without manipulators.

runtime.notes: No runtime published; battery capacity not disclosed.

battery.notes: Wireless version includes battery, but capacity and runtime not disclosed. Lite is wired only.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Official figure, added 2026-10-29 by automated spec fill; Head only (Stewart platform). No page states a total body DOF figure; P6 additionally lists a body yaw axis and 2 antenna motors, and P1's spec table lists 'Head movement (6 Degrees of Freedom)', 'Full body rotation' and '2 animated antennas'. A separate report (P2) claims 'seven flexible joints', which conflicts with these and is treated as erroneous..
degrees_of_freedom.original_value: 6 DOF: x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw (via Stewart platform)

hands.description: No hands or manipulators; only head and body rotation.

compute.description: Lite version requires an external Mac or Linux computer; Wireless version has onboard Raspberry Pi 4.

actuators.description: Not disclosed in reviewed sources. Source mentions motorized head and body rotation and animated antennas, implying motors but no detailed specifications.

availability.notes: Sold as a kit. Lite version listed at $399 (+ taxes + shipping), Wireless at $499. Launch post reported earlier price of $299 Lite and $449 Wireless per Tech Times; conflicting. Company states delivery approximately 90 days, but user comments indicate delays beyond that.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: No arms, hands, or grippers are listed in the official specifications; the robot is designed for expressive movement and interaction, not manipulation. Tech Times incorrectly described grabbing objects, conflicting with the official design.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: No evidence of autonomous task execution beyond user-controlled programs; the robot requires external compute (Lite) or onboard Raspberry Pi but no autonomy claims. The 3D voice demo space suggests interactive conversational capabilities, but that is not autonomous task execution.
caveats: No autonomy claims from official sources

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Official source lists 6 degrees of freedom for head movement and full body rotation; no walking or wheeled locomotion. Mobility is limited to upper-body/head articulation.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Official source says Reachy Mini is equipped with a wide-angle camera, four microphones, and speakers, and can use state-of-the-art open-source models for speech and vision through Hugging Face integration.
caveats: No built-in perception model demonstrated; relies on user integration

human_interaction.summary: Designed for human-robot interaction with expressive movement, microphone/speaker audio interaction, and a public 3D voice demo space showing ongoing conversational development.
caveats: No independent review of interaction quality
Demo space code indicates ongoing development

endurance_reliability.summary: No runtime, battery capacity, or reliability metrics published; company describes the product as in early development phase and sold as-is without warranties.

human_environment_fit.summary: Small desktop form factor (28 cm, 1.5 kg), intended for desk use in homes, classrooms, and labs; no locomotion or grasping, which limits physical risks.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Reachy Mini is available for purchase via Hugging Face (Lite $399, Wireless $499), and user comments indicate orders were placed, but no named commercial deployments or production use are documented.

accessibility_value.summary: Priced from $399 (Lite) and $499 (Wireless), with open-source hardware/software and Python SDK; aimed at lowering barriers for AI and robotics development.

evidence_items.title: Media-reported launch price

evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Hugging Face and Pollen Robotis have unveiled Reachy Mini, a fully programmable robot designed to accelerate AI and robotics development with accessible hardware and a starting price of only $299.

evidence_items.title: Media-reported inaccurate specifications
evidence_items.claim: Tech Times described Reachy Mini as two feet tall with seven flexible joints, stereo cameras, and object-grabbing ability, which conflicts with official specifications (28 cm, no arms/grippers).
evidence_items.notes: Tech Times appears to have used incorrect information; we do not credit these specs.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Standing at two feet tall, Reachy Mini moves with surprising grace, thanks to its seven flexible joints. It sees the world in 3D through stereo cameras, listens with built-in mics, and can do everything from carefully grabbing objects to chatting with you.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Reachy Mini is a small (28 cm, 1.5 kg) open-source desktop robot from Hugging Face and Pollen Robotics, priced at $399 (Lite) and $499 (Wireless). It features a 6-DoF motorized head, full body rotation, animated antennas, camera, microphones, and speaker, designed for human-robot interaction, education, and AI experimentation. It has no arms, hands, or locomotion, so manipulation and mobility are minimal. The robot is programmable in Python and open-source, with a growing ecosystem including a 3D voice demo Space. Evidence is mostly official and early-development; no independent verification, endurance data, or customer deployments exist. Video titles exist but without transcripts, so capabilities cannot be confirmed. Compiled automatically from public sources on 2026-10-29; requires human review.
